skillUse: Each pipeline step loads the project-authored skill that skillsByStep assigns to it, as text in that step's prompt: codebuilt-script (script), codebuilt-direction (shot list after the voice), codebuilt-scene-generation (Blender build), codebuilt-look-review (visual check). Each restates for this pipeline what the installed skills in rules.steps teach.
Only project-authored skills in this repository's .claude/skills are read. User-level skills are not loaded by the pipeline and skill text is never copied into generated code.
If a skill conflicts with the brief, the direction or the playbook, those win; say so in the report.
Only codebuilt-scene-generation is mounted into the job container, read-only, at /skills/codebuilt-scene-generation, and it is limited to one SKILL.md.

Topic skills (rules.topicSkills) are loaded only for a step they list and only when one of their keywords appears as a whole word or phrase in the topic or script; they are still guidance only and still read from this repository's .claude/skills.
playbook: Script: a story a viewer can see, hook in the first sentence, numbers instead of adjectives, one idea per sentence, every fact checked and simplifications named, a pay-off at the end.
Narration first, with per-word timestamps. Every cut, on-screen text and sound effect is placed from a word timestamp, never a guessed time.
Direction after the voice: 2 to 5 places built once, shots of 2 to 8 s cut on phrase starts, each with what is seen, what moves and how the camera moves; the view changes every 2 to 4 s.
Build every model from code in headless Blender; no downloaded assets. Ready sets and props from the kit, primitives for what is special to the story.
Pose each frame as a function of time and render it as a still, with no keyframes, so any frame renders alone and the full render splits across processes.
Preview 12 to 24 frames at half size on contact sheets, look at them, fix, repeat; most quality comes from this loop.
Subject large (a third to two thirds of the frame height) in the upper middle of the frame; captions sit low in the frame; keep text out of the top 10 percent and bottom 20 percent.
Full render at 1080x1920, 30 fps; captions word by word.
Sound: music about 18 dB under the voice and effects about 10 to 13 dB under, measured as RMS on the stems; print the numbers, never mix by guessed gains.
Check: probe the finished file, run the subtitle checker, view a contact sheet of the finished video, and report what was not verified (for example, nobody listened to the audio).
